description:
FILED s523 (Fable, 2026-10-20 21:3x) from the first red `CI` run on main after MAIN-READY-37 (e4634202, run 39469009463): the gate job fails ONE row, Pl/t/opendir-01.t row 3 `... scalar readdir and rewinddir on the original glob` -- got `. 5`, expected (perl on the runner) `.. 5`.  NOT s521e's: `%p-opendir-impl` is untouched by it.  MEASURED on this box (scratchpad od.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl at 8038fac6): on a tmpfs tempdir perl `.|.. 5` = PCL `.|.. 5`; on an ext4 tempdir (~/pcl-agent-scratch) perl `.|f3 5` vs PCL `.|.. 5` -- PCL's listing is `(list* "." ".." (mapcar #'%p-dirent-name (directory (merge-pathnames "*.*" dir-path) :resolve-symlinks nil)))`, i.e. two synthesized entries + CL's SORTED listing, while perl hands back the kernel's readdir(3) order (ext4 htree hash order; `.` and `..` wherever the fs puts them -- the runner's perl put `..` FIRST).  The row was green on every CI run until 2026-10-19/20: GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` image moved on 2026-10-19 (the run's own notice), so the runner's filesystem order changed and the order-dependent row flipped.  The dev box never sees it because File::Temp's tempdir is under /tmp = tmpfs, where both orders coincide.  THE FIX (one function, cl/): list through `sb-posix:opendir` / `sb-posix:readdir` / `sb-posix:closedir` -- the names in the order the kernel gives, `.` and `..` included as the kernel includes them, nothing synthesized, nothing sorted (perl semantics EXACTLY, and `telldir`/`seekdir` keep their index model over that list); keep `%p-literal-path`'s no-wildcard handling for the DIRECTORY name and the #2922 errno path (the sb-posix opendir is already called once for No such file or directory; reuse that stream for the listing -- rule 11).  GUARD: a Pl/t row comparing the FULL raw `readdir` order with perl on a directory ON THE CHECKOUT'S FILESYSTEM (a tempdir under ``, never /tmp), inverse-fails on 8038fac6 on ext4; opendir-01.t row 3 then passes on any filesystem UNCHANGED (do not rewrite it).  Also probe: `readdir` in list context after a partial scalar read, `rewinddir`, a directory with 50 entries (htree), a symlink entry (name, not target), a directory deleted after opendir.  Companion: io/ files that list directories (`io/fs.t`? `op/readdir.t` = the one to run), the sweep's perl-tests covering opendir.  Handed to s523a as a FILLER (first) because its batch is already a cl/ batch with the sweep in its legs; CI on main stays red until it merges (one round).

=== DONE (s523a, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-20) ===
FIX (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, one function + a helper): %p-opendir-impl lists through the opendir(3) stream it already opens for the #2922 errno path (rule 11 -- the stream that used to be closed at once is now the one read): new %p-dir-stream-names = sb-posix:readdir until the null dirent, sb-posix:dirent-name each, closedir in an unwind-protect.  Nothing synthesized, nothing sorted; `telldir`/`seekdir`/`rewinddir` keep the index model over that list; the CL DIRECTORY call, the merged "*.*" pattern and the probe-file are gone (opendir(3) takes the directory name literally, so #755's `*`-in-the-name case needs no %p-literal-path here).
PROBE scratch/s523a/pr/rd.pl (a tempdir under the worktree = ext4): full list order (files + subdir + symlink), partial scalar reads then list, rewinddir first entry, telldir/seekdir, closedir twice (1 / undef), a 52-entry directory, the symlink listed by its own name, opendir of a missing dir ($! ENOENT) -- perl = tree; base differs on the three ORDER lines (sorted with . .. first).
GUARD Pl/t/opendir-01.t row 9 (new; rows 1-8 unchanged, row 3 untouched): the full raw readdir order + rewinddir/rest count of a 55-entry directory created under $RealBin (the checkout's filesystem), compared with perl -- FAILS on the 8038fac6 extraction, passes on the tree.
Targeted gate: the 15 Pl/t files that use opendir/readdir pass.  op/readdir.t joins s523a's exclusive companion run; the sweep is in s523a's legs.
subject: readdir ORDER is synthesized (".", "..", then `directory`'s sorted names) where perl returns the KERNEL's order -- Pl/t/opendir-01.t row 3 compares the first raw entry and went RED on CI (ubuntu-latest image change of 2026-10-19), green on the box because /tmp is tmpfs
